title: The electronics ‘under the hood’ of space networking

summary: Space Angel received a $1.75 million grant from the Western Australian Government to advance plans for a spaceport. The funding was announced by Science and Innovation Minister Stephen Dawson.

summary: Tendeg unveiled NewTEN, a two-axis steerable compact antenna designed to enhance communications performance and pointing access for small spacecraft. The product was introduced at the SmallSat event in Salt Lake City.

summary: Spirit Electronics expanded its online store to include space-grade components from Texas Instruments and Microchip Technology ahead of SmallSat 2026. This move aims to support high-reliability electronics for space applications.

summary: The article discusses the importance of technology and talent for future cislunar exploration, building on past achievements like the Apollo moon landing. It highlights the ongoing relevance of these advancements for scientific and national security progress.

summary: Astronomers discovered the first Kuiper Belt object beyond Pluto on Aug. 30, 1992. The object, named 1992 QB-1, marked a significant milestone in understanding the outer solar system.

summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched into space atop a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket on Aug. 30, marking a significant advancement for astronomy. The mission aims to deepen our understanding of the cosmos.

summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope is scheduled to launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket on August 30. The mission aims to advance astronomical discoveries.

title: When is the next lunar eclipse?
summary: The next lunar eclipse after the August 2026 partial lunar eclipse will occur on March 3, 2026, as a penumbral lunar eclipse. Earth's shadow will next fully cover the moon during a total lunar eclipse on March 14, 2025.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 29, 1965: NASA's Gemini 5 breaks spaceflight duration record after 2 astronauts spent '8 days in a garbage can'
summary: NASA's Gemini 5 mission concluded on Aug. 29, 1965, after two astronauts spent eight days in space, breaking the spaceflight duration record. The mission paved the way for future lunar trips.

summary: SpaceX successfully test-fired all 33 engines of its Super Heavy booster, preparing for the upcoming Starship Flight 14, which aims to achieve orbital flight for the first time.

title: Meeting Nancy Grace Roman: What was the 'mother of Hubble' really like?
summary: The article discusses a personal encounter with Nancy Grace Roman, known as the 'mother of Hubble,' highlighting her significance in astronomy. It reflects on her legacy nearly a decade after the meeting.

summary: NASA's Deep Space Network has added a new 34-meter antenna, DSS-23, at its Goldstone complex in California, enhancing deep space communications capabilities. The multifrequency beam-waveguide antenna is expected to boost the DSN's capacity for decades.

summary: NASA's Deep Space Network (DSN) Goldstone complex features five 34-meter antennas, including the recently completed Deep Space Station 23. The image showcases the antennas under the summer sun near Barstow, California, in August 2026.

title: NASA’s Dark Universe-Seeking Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Launches
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket to study the universe's dark secrets. The mission will take three months to reach its final orbit, a million miles from Earth.

title: NASA’s Artemis II Crew Receives Congressional Space Medal of Honor
summary: NASA's Artemis II crew, including astronauts Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen, and Reid Wiseman, received the Congressional Space Medal of Honor from President Donald Trump in 2026 for their contributions to the Artemis II mission.

title: NASA Awards First Prize in Phase 2 of Agency’s LunaRecycle Challenge
summary: NASA awarded the first prize in Phase 2 of its LunaRecycle Challenge to MIT's CERBERUZ team for developing a technology to recycle waste materials like fabrics, plastics, and metals during lunar or deep space missions. The team received $775,000 in awards for their innovative trash-recycling solution.

summary: President Donald Trump awarded NASA and CSA astronauts with the Congressional Space Medal of Honor for their roles in the Artemis II mission. The ceremony took place at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston.

summary: President Trump signed an executive order to establish the U.S. Space Academy, aiming to strengthen the nation's space workforce and develop future space leaders. The academy is intended to support national security, economic growth, scientific discovery, and technological innovation.

title: Grants

summary: APOD features an astronomy image of the sky above Paranal Observatory on August 28, 2026. The daily astronomy feature includes a professional astronomer's explanation of the cosmic phenomenon.

summary: NASA and SpaceX successfully launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida. This marks a significant milestone in space observatory missions.

summary: The Soyuz MS-28 spacecraft departed from the International Space Station. Three spacewalks were conducted to install upgrades to the station's solar arrays and antennae.

summary: Starbase's production site is experiencing increased activity to boost future production capacity. The site is a key facility for SpaceX's development and manufacturing operations.

summary: Falcon Heavy is set to launch the Roman Space Telescope, while Falcon 9 will deploy Starlink satellites this week. Five orbital launches are planned from China, the United States, and French Guiana.

summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is nearing its launch date of August 30 after reaching final integration and rehearsal milestones.

summary: LandSpace's Zhuque-3 rocket toppled after achieving a significant milestone with its first stage landing. This marks a critical step for China's commercial space industry.

summary: Ship 41 has completed engine testing in preparation for Flight 14. Ship 40 is being transported back to Starbase from Christmas Island.

This development highlights progress in reusable launch vehicle technology amid competition in the space industry.

summary: The news source is a B2B website focused on the technology, engineering, and construction sectors, covering business-related content.

summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft designed for microgravity experiments and safe Earth return.

summary: Proba-3 is set to observe a double eclipse, where the Moon crosses its field of view. This event highlights the satellite's advanced observational capabilities.

summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona, which is otherwise difficult to study due to the rarity and brief duration of natural eclipses.

summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This presents a unique opportunity for testing and demonstrating innovative software in a deep-space environment.

summary: SpaceX announced a new high-cadence launch site in Louisiana for future Starship operations, with Gwynne Shotwell and Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry present at the announcement.

summary: OrbitAID plans to launch a rendezvous and proximity operations (RPO) demonstration in 2027, aiming to validate the entire satellite life extension process in a single mission. Most previous RPO demonstrations have only tested isolated aspects of the sequence.

summary: Kepler Communications has partnered with NorthStar to combine its optical data relay infrastructure with NorthStar's Space Domain Awareness services. The strategic partnership was announced on Thursday.
